reason: The cited evidence (E1) only shows that phosphorus broadens the solidification range and promotes amorphization under rapid cooling; it provides no data on the as-quenched microstructure, sub-Tg atomic mobility, phosphorus homogenization, or its effect on crystallization kinetics and supercooled liquid region width. All key premises beyond the general amorphization tendency are unsupported.
premises: Phosphorus promotes amorphization in CrMnFeCoNi-P alloys under rapid cooling
As-quenched Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 contains localized phosphorus enrichment
Sub-Tg annealing (Tg–30 K, 10 min) allows atomic mobility sufficient to homogenize phosphorus without crystallization
Homogenizing phosphorus distribution increases the nucleation barrier for crystallization
Increased nucleation barrier widens the supercooled liquid region by 10–20%
